### Relationships Between Modifications

The modifications in both files are related as they address the same issue of type inconsistency for the `max_threads` variable. The change in `binder.c` ensures that the value copied from user space matches the new `__u32` type defined for the `BINDER_SET_MAX_THREADS` ioctl. Simultaneously, the change in `binder_internal.h` updates the internal representation of `max_threads` in the `binder_proc` structure to maintain consistency across the codebase. Together, these changes prevent potential incompatibility issues between 32-bit and 64-bit kernels.

Here is the commit message:
binder: fix max_thread type inconsistency
MIME-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8
Content-Transfer-Encoding: 8bit

The type defined for the BINDER_SET_MAX_THREADS ioctl was changed from
size_t to __u32 in order to avoid incompatibility issues between 32 and
64-bit kernels. However, the internal types used to copy from user and
store the value were never updated. Use u32 to fix the inconsistency.

Fixes: a9350fc859ae ("staging: android: binder: fix BINDER_SET_MAX_THREADS declaration")
Reported-by: Arve Hjønnevåg <arve@android.com>
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Carlos Llamas <cmllamas@google.com>
Reviewed-by: Alice Ryhl <aliceryhl@google.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20240421173750.3117808-1-cmllamas@google.com
Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by a type inconsistency between the `BINDER_SET_MAX_THREADS` ioctl definition, which was changed to `__u32`, and the internal handling of the `max_threads` variable, which was still defined as `int`. This inconsistency could lead to incorrect data being processed, especially when interacting with user space, potentially causing issues in 32-bit and 64-bit kernel compatibility.

Here is the patch:
 	struct binder_stats stats;
 	struct list_head delivered_death;
-	int max_threads;
+	u32 max_threads;
 	int requested_threads;
 	int requested_threads_started;

This inconsistency can lead to incorrect data handling, especially when the value is passed between user space and kernel space, potentially causing issues in 32-bit and 64-bit kernel compatibility.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
+	u32 max_threads;
```
Reason:
Changing the type of `max_threads` from `int` to `u32` aligns it with the `BINDER_SET_MAX_THREADS` ioctl definition. This ensures that the data types are consistent, preventing potential data corruption and compatibility issues when interacting with user space, thus resolving the bug.
